findings.passage: There are things that we can and should do to increase firearms safety in Wisconsin, like passing universal background checks, requiring safe and secure storage of firearms, and tightening up the training requirements for concealed carry permit holders.
findings.note: Official press release after the Assembly passed bills expanding concealed carry. She names universal background checks, safe storage and carry-permit training as steps to take.

findings.passage: These are a dangerous combination of bills, allowing 18 year olds to get concealed carry permits and allowing permit holders to have firearms in their vehicles on school grounds. In addition, opening up a loophole where out-of-state individuals don’t need a background check to receive a Wisconsin concealed carry permit will not improve safety.
findings.note: Objects to AB 498 (age 18 for carry permits), AB 495 (permit holders' guns in vehicles on school grounds) and AB 518 (out-of-state permit holders getting a permit without a background check).

findings.passage: I come from a family of hunters going back generations and I understand the place that hunting and firearms have in our state’s cultural heritage. But I also understand that carrying and using a firearm requires great care, caution, and practice to handle them in a safe and responsible manner.
findings.note: General statement on firearms and hunting heritage alongside a call for safe handling.
